xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4578: Sync operator-level memory across machines (follow-up to PAN-3957)

plan.title: Sync operator-level memory across machines (follow-up to PAN-3957)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: PAN-3957 keeps operator facts (working agreements about the operator) in ~/.overdeck/context/memory/ on each machine and lists syncing as a non-goal. The operator works across several machines, so an operator fact written on one machine never reaches the others. The operator store also doubles as the home for machine-specific facts (home-directory paths), which must not travel.
narratives.Proposal: Make the operator store a plain git clone of a private repository the operator owns (`pan memory sync --setup <git-url>`; no config key, the clone's origin is the setting). syncOperatorMemory commits local changes (holding back secret-like or home-path files), fetches, merges origin/main and pushes, never throwing; conflicts keep the remote version under the id and commit a review-marked `<id>-conflict-<machine>` copy of the local version. Add a never-synced machine store (~/.overdeck/context/machine-memory/, --machine, ## Machine memory) and apply the home-path guard to the operator store. Sync runs from `pan memory sync`, `pan sync` (before --if-changed), a 15-minute dashboard timer, and after `--user` writes; never at launch.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Encrypting operator facts or storing them in the Session Vault
- Creating the sync repository, checking it is private, or managing git credentials
- Syncing the machine store, the project store, the global layer, or anything else under ~/.overdeck
- Any network access, fetch or git process at launch time (render.ts, materialize.ts, muse-context.ts)
- A dashboard UI for sync setup, status or conflicts
- Automatically merging fact content in a conflict (the operator resolves conflict copies)
- More than one remote, or a branch other than main
- A --no-sync flag on add/edit/retire --user
- Changing the project store, observation memory, PAN-3957 D17 pipeline carve-outs, or OKF
- Implementing PAN-4577 (W11 only amends its plan unless the checkpoint finds it landed)
- git stash, reset --hard or execSync anywhere
- Running pan sync on the host as part of the work

autoDecisions.summary: Q1: the operator store becomes a plain git clone of an operator-owned private repo, set up with `pan memory sync --setup <git-url>`; no config key (origin is the setting).
autoDecisions.rationale: It is the issue's own example ('a private git repository that pan sync pulls and pushes'); facts stay readable OKF-compatible markdown; D10 already refuses secret-like text, so the Session Vault's encryption buys little and would make facts opaque; storing the URL in config would duplicate what git already records.

autoDecisions.summary: Q2: machine-specific facts move to a new never-synced machine store ~/.overdeck/context/machine-memory/ (--machine), and the home-path guard now applies to the operator store; setup migrates existing home-path operator facts.
autoDecisions.rationale: git cannot ignore files by content and the reader already skips subdirectories, so a sibling directory needs no exclude list and no second reader; the operator store now travels, so PAN-3957 D16's reasoning applies to it; 0 operator facts exist on this host, so nothing is stranded here.

autoDecisions.summary: Q3: on a conflict the remote version keeps the id and the local version is committed as a review-marked <id>-conflict-<machine-label> fact; an edit beats a deletion.
autoDecisions.rationale: Nothing is lost, an unattended sync never blocks on conflict markers, and PAN-3957's review marker already keeps such a fact out of the index, so no new state is invented. Last-writer-wins by the day-granularity updated date would silently lose same-day edits.

autoDecisions.summary: Sync triggers: pan memory sync, pan sync (placed before the --if-changed early return), a 15-minute dashboard timer, and once after each --user write; never at launch.
autoDecisions.rationale: pan sync --if-changed returns before any step when only the remote changed, so a step after it would never pull; the timer covers long-running machines; post-write sync makes an agent-recorded fact reach other machines without waiting; the launch path is synchronous and must never touch the network (PAN-3957 D9).

autoDecisions.summary: The dashboard service calls syncOperatorMemory in-process (async execFile) instead of spawning the pan CLI.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every git call is async execFile, so no-execsync-server holds; the library is self-contained and a CLI spawn would add a process per tick for no isolation benefit; a dynamic import avoids circular ESM edges like sync-auto-service.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: PAN-4577's plan is amended in .pan/drafts/pan-3957.md W9 (home-path imports go to the machine store) and PAN-4577 gets a comment, with an implementation checkpoint if its code has already landed.
autoDecisions.rationale: After this issue the operator store refuses home-path facts, so PAN-4577's planned routing would fail at writeMemoryFact; fixing the plan text now prevents a broken import.

metadata.sizeJustification: One vertical feature that crosses its natural seams once each: the fact store (new scope), the launch renderer, the Context preview the docs promise matches it, the pan memory CLI door (which must regenerate the composer manifest and skill in lockstep), the new sync library and its conflict module, the pan sync step, the dashboard timer, the PAN-4577 plan amendment, and docs. About 27 files, half of them tests and docs each slice carries; the subsystem count is inflated by tests/, sync-sources/, configuration/, packages/ and root docs files. Splitting the machine store from the sync would ship a synced operator store that pushes machine-specific facts to other machines, or a guard that strands facts with nowhere to go; splitting the dashboard timer out would ship a sync that never pulls on a long-running machine.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD W6 (D10): export resolveSyncConflicts({ dir, labelSlug, git }) and conflictCopyId(id, labelSlug). For each unmerged path read stages via git ls-files -u -z: both stages -> checkout --theirs and, for a top-level <id>.md other than README.md, write the conflict copy from `git show :2:<path>`; only ours -> checkout --ours; only theirs -> checkout --theirs; then git add. Conflict copy id = id.slice(0, 80 - suffix.length) + suffix with suffix '-conflict-' + labelSlug; content = serializeMemoryFact of the parsed local fact with review de-duplicated [...review, 'sync-conflict'] and source 'sync-conflict:<id>', or the raw local bytes when it does not parse. In operator-sync.ts replace exactly the pre-W6 abort branch with the resolver call plus `git commit --no-edit` (identity flags) and fill outcome.conflicts. Replace W5's abort test with the both-versions-kept test.
